integration_questions: Did the 12 cm span with seven sensors cause any saturation or reduced resolution on the sharpest bends compared with the 6 cm span?
Did the 16 mm footprint produce a smoother signal, or did it blur the edges and add oscillation?
Did the 0.6 kg mass reduce or increase the steering oscillation at higher base speeds?
At which track and which point in the course does max_error reach its peak, and does line loss happen at the same place?
Is the seven-sensor weight pattern easy to tune, and which sensors carry most of the signal?
feedback_request.requested_format: Brief notes on each question, plus the one geometry change you would make first if you could change only one thing.

intent: Change sensing breadth and inertia together to test whether they reduce off-track excursions. Widen the sensor span from 6 cm to 12 cm with seven sensors at 2 cm spacing, enlarge the footprint to 16 mm, lower mass to 0.6 kg, and move the sensors slightly forward to y = 0.06 m. Expect max_error below the 0.06 m limit on the development tracks, fewer line-loss events, and a first completed run on at least one development track.
learning: Iteration 0 showed that every run left the track through max_error above 0.06 m, so the next design should reduce peak excursion, not average error. Hypotheses to test: (1) a 12 cm sensor span reduces line-loss events on slalom and s-bend; (2) a 16 mm footprint gives a smoother signal near the edges; (3) lower mass reduces the time to correct a large error. Measurements to request: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort on each development track.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced with no completions: all 60 trials ended off track, with progress between 0.12 and 0.19. The per-track mean rms_error was small (0.024 to 0.030 m), but max_error reached 0.061 to 0.064 m, above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Line-loss events were 1.0 to 1.55 per run. The failures come from occasional large excursions, not from steady tracking error. Body width cannot widen the limit: max(0.06, 0.0125 + width/4) stays at 0.06 for every width up to 0.18 m, so the only lever is to keep max_error below 0.06. Line loss on bends suggests the 6 cm sensor span is too narrow to keep tape under a sensor. I am therefore widening the span to 0.12 m with seven sensors at 0.02 m spacing, which covers about 4.8 tape widths and should keep the line visible through larger lateral error. I am also moving to 16 mm footprints, so each sensor overlaps the tape over a wider range and gives a more graded reading. The sensors stay forward at y = 0.06 m to keep the lead distance. I am lowering mass to 0.6 kg to reduce yaw inertia and speed up turn response, and keeping wheel track, wheel radius and body size at baseline so that the change in each run can be attributed to a small number of variables. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, lower max_error, and at least some completions on the oval and s-bend tracks. Main risk: the 16 mm footprint may blur edges and the lower mass may increase oscillation at speed.
